title: Imjin War (Japanese invasions of Korea)
summary: From 1592 to 1598 Toyotomi Hideyoshi's armies invaded Korea, aiming to conquer Ming China. They took Seoul and Pyongyang in 1592, but Admiral Yi Sun-sin's navy, Ming troops and Korean irregulars stalled the advance. A second invasion in 1597 fared worse, and Japan withdrew after Hideyoshi died in September 1598.

uncertainty.note: The army sailed in May 1592; Hideyoshi died in September 1598 and the invasion was abandoned.

as_recorded.value: The two Japanese invasions of Korea between 1592 and 1598 CE, otherwise known as the Imjin Wars
invaded Chosŏn Korea in 1592 ... the Imjin War ended after the Japanese withdrew their troops from Korea in 1598

where.historical_name: Pusan (Busan), fort and port at the southeast tip of the Korean peninsula, Joseon Korea

importance.justification: One of the largest military operations in East Asia before the 20th century, with lasting effects on Korea, China and Japan.

audience_note: Describes mass killing, mutilation of victims and the removal of prisoners.

beats.caption: A Japanese army landed near Busan in May 1592, took Seoul on 12 June and Pyongyang on 23 July.
The first invasion stalled in 1593 under pressure from the Korean navy, Ming troops and local rebels.
Hideyoshi died in September 1598 and Japan withdrew; one estimate counts at least 125,000 Korean deaths.

reviewer_note: Least sure of casualty and force figures: World History Encyclopedia gives 158,000 invaders plus 9,200 mariners in 1592 and at least 125,000 Korean dead; the UCLA essay says only that hundreds of thousands fought. Pyongyang coordinates are a Wikidata point.
